title: Three Oaks Bakery: a monthly box?
question: Should our three bakeries offer a monthly subscription box, and if so, what shape should it take?
summary: Three Oaks is a small chain of three bakeries. Regulars have asked for a box they can collect or have delivered each month. This canvas shows what a subscriber would go through, what the shop would have to do behind the counter, where the idea comes from, and what is still open. All names and numbers are made up.

checked.note: Checked against six customer chats, 64 survey slips, a four-week waste log, a year of sales and costs, the till supplier call, three other local boxes, and one staff meeting.

roles.label: Designer
roles.asks: Will people understand this and find their way without help?
jobs: Make signing up take under two minutes at the counter or online

roles.label: Analyst
roles.asks: Is it clear what must be true, for whom, and how we will measure it?

roles.label: Head baker
roles.asks: Can we bake and pack this without breaking the weekend?
jobs: Keep the Friday and weekend bake on time

roles.label: Owner
roles.asks: What is in the first version, what do we cut, and what does success look like?

roles.label: Privacy
roles.asks: What customer details do we keep, who sees them, and for how long?

roles.label: Customer voice
roles.asks: Would our regulars choose this, and would they need it explained?
jobs: Get good bread without thinking about it

roles.label: AI agent teammate
roles.asks: What could an assistant do on its own, and what needs a person's OK?

roles.label: Finance
roles.asks: What does it cost to run, and when does it pay back?

reading: Start with the list on the left. The first view follows a subscriber through signing up, a normal month, and asking for help or leaving. The second view shows the same box from behind the counter: baking, packing, collection and money. The third view traces the idea from what customers said to what we would launch, and whether it worked; switch between Today and Planned to see what exists and what we propose. Each box says whether it works today, partly works, is missing, or is planned. Notes from the owner, head baker, finance and others sit on the boxes they are about; each ends in a question for the team to answer.

glossary.churn: The share of subscribers who cancel in a given month.
glossary.margin: What is left from the price after ingredients, packaging, fees and staff time.
glossary.packing list: The sheet that says how many boxes, of which size and with which swaps, to pack for a given day.
glossary.stored card: A customer's card kept by the till so it can be charged again without them being there.
glossary.declined: A card charge the bank refused, for example because the card expired.

evidence.text: I'd pay for a box if I could skip a month when we're away. I hate being locked in.
Friday treats for the team would be great, but I need an invoice, not a card charge.
What's in it each month? I don't want six things I won't eat.
If there's nothing for me, I'm out.
£25 a month feels right. £35 feels like a treat I'd cancel.
A trial box costs £11.40 in ingredients and packaging, plus about 14 minutes of staff time to pack.
9% of baked goods are thrown away or given away at closing.
Local courier: £4.20 per drop within 3 miles, Tuesday or Friday only.
Friday afternoon is already our tightest time.
The counter team can take sign-ups but not chase failed payments.
Roughly 380 customers visit at least once a week.
Nobody owns the customer list today. Loyalty data lives in the till system.
Monday waste is 13% of what is baked; Saturday is 5%.
Ovens sit idle from 1pm to 4pm Monday to Thursday.
Early-week waste is mostly sourdough and seeded loaves.
41 of 64 regulars said they would probably or definitely try a monthly box.
Of those 41, 29 prefer collecting and 12 prefer delivery.
24 of 64 ticked £25 as a fair price; only 8 ticked £30 or more.
11 of 64 (17%) avoid gluten, nuts or dairy.
19 of 64 would want to skip at least one month a year.
Let me choose the bread.
Text me, don't email me.
Would buy one as a gift.
If a stored-card charge fails, the till marks it declined in a daily report. It does not retry and does not tell the customer.
The till can send a text through an add-on at 4p per message.
Any staff login can see every customer's name, phone, email and points.
The till cannot raise invoices. The office buyer is invoiced by hand, about 20 minutes a month.
All three local boxes show a photo of this month's box on their front page.
The cheese shop lets people skip any month online before the 20th; the veg box allows four weeks of pause a year.
None of the three offer an allergy swap.
Owner wants the box to cut waste, not add to it, and proposes baking box items on Thursday.
Idea: let subscribers pick up on Saturday, when shops are busy anyway.

gaps.title: Let people pause a month
gaps.why: The first thing a regular asked for, and 19 of 64 survey slips want it. Without it, people avoid signing up.

stories.as: As a subscriber going on holiday, I want to skip next month by replying to a text, so I am not charged for bread I cannot collect.
done_when: a reply of SKIP before Wednesday stops that month's charge
the Saturday packing list leaves that person out
the subscriber gets a text confirming the skip

stories.as: As the Mill Lane manager, I want to see who skipped this month, so we bake the right number on Thursday.
done_when: the Thursday packing list shows the count of skips
skips made at the counter appear on the list the same day

gaps.title: Say what is in the box, and offer a gluten-free swap
gaps.why: People will not pay for things they cannot eat; one in six avoid gluten, nuts or dairy; no other local box offers a swap.

stories.as: As a new customer, I want to see this month's box before I sign up, so I know it suits us.
done_when: a photo and list are at the counter from the first Monday of the month
the reminder text on the 25th says what is coming next month

stories.as: As a gluten-free regular, I want a swap packed for me every month, so I can stay a subscriber.
done_when: the diet need is asked once at sign-up
the packing list marks each swap
swap boxes sit on their own labelled shelf

stories.as: As the head baker, I want swaps baked in a separate batch, so there is no cross-contact.
done_when: swaps are baked first on a cleaned tray
they cool on a separate rack and go straight into labelled bags

gaps.title: Someone owns failed payments
gaps.why: The till does not retry or tell the customer, and the counter team cannot chase.

stories.as: As a subscriber whose card expired, I want a text asking me to update it, so my box is not missed.
done_when: a text goes out the day a charge is declined
the box is held, not packed, until the charge goes through
a second text goes on day 3, then we stop

stories.as: As the Mill Lane manager, I want one short list of declined charges each morning, so it takes two minutes.
done_when: the list shows only subscribers, not all card payments
each line has name, phone and amount

gaps.title: Invoices for office buyers
gaps.why: Office buyers need an invoice; the till cannot make one and hand-written invoices take 20 minutes a month.

stories.as: As an office buyer, I want a monthly invoice with our company name, so I can claim it back.
done_when: an invoice goes out on the 1st with the company name and order
it shows the shop's VAT number if we have one

gaps.title: Gift boxes
gaps.why: Five survey slips asked for gifts, and gifts bring in new customers.

stories.as: As a customer, I want to buy three months for my mum in one payment, so she gets bread without paying.
done_when: one up-front payment covers three boxes
the gift ends by itself after three months

stories.as: As the person receiving a gift, I want to be asked before I get texts, so I don't feel signed up behind my back.
done_when: the first text asks them to reply YES to get reminders
if they don't reply, the counter tells them at their first pickup

gaps.title: A rule for boxes not collected
gaps.why: Boxes left on the shelf become waste, and the box is meant to cut waste.

stories.as: As a subscriber who forgot, I want my box kept until Sunday, so I can still get it.
done_when: uncollected boxes stay on the shelf until Sunday closing
on Monday they go to the food charity, with no refund

notes.title: Pausing decides whether people sign up
notes.body: The regular who asked for this said being locked in is the reason they would say no.
notes.recommend: Make pausing a one-word text reply, and say so on the counter card.
notes.question: Do we let people pause as often as they like, or cap it at two months a year?

notes.title: Show a real box at the counter
notes.body: People asked what is inside before they asked the price.
notes.recommend: Put a packed sample box by the till with a card listing this month's items.
notes.question: Who packs and refreshes the sample box each month?

notes.title: Friday packing clashes with the weekend bake
notes.body: The head baker named Friday afternoon as the tightest time of the week.
notes.recommend: Pack Thursday evening for Saturday pickup; no Friday deliveries in the pilot.
notes.question: Can we commit to Saturday-only pickup for the first eight weeks?

notes.title: The box makes money at £25, but not with delivery
notes.body: Ingredients, packaging and packing time come to about £14. Card fees take another 43p. Delivery at £4.20 leaves little.
notes.recommend: Price at £25 for collection and £29 with delivery once delivery starts.
notes.question: Are we happy with roughly £10 a box before rent and power?

notes.title: Pilot in one shop first
notes.body: Mill Lane has the most regulars asking. A cap keeps the bake manageable.
notes.recommend: Pilot at Mill Lane, cap at 30 boxes, review after eight weeks.
notes.question: What number of subscribers after eight weeks would make us roll it out to all three shops?

notes.title: Agree the measures before we start
notes.body: Without a starting number for waste, we cannot say the box reduced it.
notes.recommend: Record this month's waste at Mill Lane as the starting point.
notes.question: Which three numbers do we review at week eight?

notes.title: Keep as little customer data as we can
notes.body: We would hold names, phone numbers and cards. Nobody owns the customer list today.
notes.recommend: Keep cards in the payment provider only, and name one person responsible for the list.
notes.question: Who owns the subscriber list, and how long do we keep details after someone cancels?

notes.title: An assistant could send the reminders and handle skips
notes.body: Reminder texts, skip replies and the packing list follow simple rules.
notes.recommend: Let an assistant send reminders and record skips; a person approves the weekly packing list.
notes.question: Are we comfortable with an assistant replying to customers' texts about skips?

notes.title: Office buyers are a different customer
notes.body: They want Friday treats and an invoice, not a personal card charge.
notes.recommend: Leave office boxes out of the pilot; talk to three office buyers first.
notes.question: Do we treat office boxes as a separate product later?

notes.title: Failed payments cost more than the fee
notes.body: A packed box nobody paid for is £14 lost.
notes.recommend: Hold the box until the payment goes through.
notes.question: Do we pack boxes for people whose payment failed, or hold them?

notes.title: Ask about dietary needs once, at sign-up
notes.body: A box with nothing someone can eat is the fastest way to lose them.
notes.recommend: One question at sign-up with three choices: none, gluten-free, no nuts.
notes.question: Can the bakery reliably make a gluten-free swap every month?

notes.title: Thursday baking uses spare oven time
notes.body: Weekday sales are well below weekends, so Thursday has room.
notes.recommend: Bake box items Thursday afternoon; freeze dough on Wednesday if needed.
notes.question: Does a Thursday bake keep the bread good enough for Saturday?

notes.title: Define the skip deadline
notes.body: Packing happens Thursday, so a skip on Friday is too late.
notes.recommend: Skips close at the end of Wednesday.
notes.question: Is Wednesday a fair deadline for skipping?

notes.title: Invoices can wait
notes.body: Only one buyer asked, and invoices need more admin than the pilot can carry.
notes.recommend: Do invoices after the pilot if office demand is real.
notes.question: Do we say no to office buyers during the pilot?

notes.title: A photo sells it better than words
notes.body: All three local boxes lead with a photo; our regulars ask what is in it before anything else.
notes.recommend: Frame a photo of this month's box by each till, changed on the first Monday.
notes.question: Who takes the photo and changes the frame each month?

notes.title: Make skipping one word
notes.body: People said 'text me'; a one-word reply is easier than any form.
notes.recommend: Reply SKIP to the reminder text; confirm by text.
notes.question: Is a text reply enough, or do we also need a way to skip at the counter?

notes.title: Diet needs must be on the packing list
notes.body: If the diet note lives only in the till, packers will not see it on Friday morning.
notes.recommend: Print the diet need next to each name on the packing list.
notes.question: Which diet needs do we support at launch: gluten-free only, or nuts and dairy too?

notes.title: Uncollected boxes need a rule before launch
notes.body: Without a rule, counter staff will each do something different.
notes.recommend: Keep until Sunday closing, then give to the food charity; no refund.
notes.question: Do we refund an uncollected box, or not?

notes.title: Gluten-free swaps need their own batch
notes.body: Baking swaps alongside normal loaves risks cross-contact; we cannot promise 'free from' today.
notes.recommend: Bake swaps first on a cleaned tray and call them 'made without gluten', not 'gluten-free'.
notes.question: Are we willing to promise gluten-free, or only 'made without gluten'?

notes.title: Packing time must come down
notes.body: 14 minutes a box is close to four hours for 15 boxes on a Friday morning.
notes.recommend: Set up a packing table with pre-folded boxes and labels printed from the list.
notes.question: Can we get packing under 8 minutes a box before we pass 15 subscribers?

notes.title: The box is for steady midweek income
notes.body: The point is to bake to a known number on quiet days, not to sell more on busy ones.
notes.recommend: Judge the pilot on midweek waste and steady income, not on total sales.
notes.question: Do we agree the pilot is judged on waste and steady income first?

notes.title: Gifts can wait until after the pilot
notes.body: Gifts bring new people in, but they add a second person's details and a different payment.
notes.recommend: Collect names of people who ask for gifts and come back to them at week eight.
notes.question: Do we take gift requests during the pilot or say 'soon'?

notes.title: Every staff login can see every customer
notes.body: The till shows names, phones and emails to any login; adding subscribers adds more people at risk.
notes.recommend: Turn on separate logins for managers and counter staff before launch.
notes.question: Can the till limit who sees customer phone numbers?

notes.title: A gift means holding someone else's number
notes.body: The person receiving a gift has not agreed to be texted.
notes.recommend: Ask the receiver to reply YES before any reminder texts.
notes.question: Are we comfortable storing a gift receiver's phone without asking them first?

notes.title: People want to choose their bread
notes.body: Seven slips asked to choose the bread; it was the most common free comment.
notes.recommend: Offer a choice of two loaves each month at sign-up, not a full menu.
notes.question: Is a choice of two loaves enough, or does it need to change month by month?

notes.title: Collecting is fine for most
notes.body: 29 of 41 interested people prefer collecting; delivery would be nice but not paid for.
notes.recommend: Launch with Saturday collection only.
notes.question: Do we offer delivery later only if 10 or more subscribers ask?

notes.title: An assistant could send the first payment reminder
notes.body: The till marks declines but tells nobody; a short text could go out the same morning.
notes.recommend: Let an assistant send one polite text per decline; a person handles replies.
notes.question: Do we let an assistant text customers about payments, or only about pickups?

notes.title: An assistant could prepare the packing list
notes.body: The list is a filter of the till report: active, paid, not skipped, with swaps.
notes.recommend: Have it ready by 8am Thursday for the head baker to check.
notes.question: Who checks the list before the bake, and what if it looks wrong?

notes.title: Delivery costs more than it earns
notes.body: £4.20 a drop on a £25 box takes margin from about £10 to under £6.
notes.recommend: Charge delivery at cost, or leave it out of the pilot.
notes.question: If we add delivery later, do we charge £4 or absorb it?

notes.title: Track the box as its own line
notes.body: Without a monthly line we cannot tell whether the box pays for itself.
notes.recommend: One line a month: boxes, revenue, ingredients, packing minutes, waste.
notes.question: Who fills in the monthly line, and when do we look at it?

notes.title: The counter script keeps answers the same
notes.body: Different staff gave different answers about contents and price.
notes.recommend: Print a three-line script on the back of the packing list.
notes.question: Who writes the script, and who checks it each month?

notes.title: A gift text should feel like a gift
notes.body: The first message is the whole experience for a gift receiver.
notes.recommend: Say who it is from and when to collect, in one short text.
notes.question: Do we show the giver's name in the text?

decisions.question: Do we run an eight-week pilot at Mill Lane, collection only, capped at 30 boxes?
What price do we start at?
How do pausing and failed payments work?
options: Two pauses a year, hold unpaid boxes

decisions.question: Do we promise 'gluten-free' or 'made without gluten'?
options: Made without gluten, with a clear warning

decisions.question: Who can see subscribers' phone numbers?

outcomes.measure: Cancellations in the first two months
Declined charges sorted within three days
